The speed for an arbitrary radius R between the tabulated values R~j~ and R~j+1~ is obtained by linear interpolation:

$$V_p(R) = V_j + \frac{R - R_j}{R_{j+1} - R_j}\,(V_{j+1} - V_j) \le \max V_r$$
Zakonitost V~p~ – i~N~ ograničava brzinu: The V~p~ – i~N~ relationship limits the speed in the cases: {0}; most unfavourable in case {1} ({2}), where the grade in the direction of travel reaches {3} %
Na osnovu rezultirajućeg profila V~p~(s):
On the basis of the resulting profile V~p~(s) on a section of length L, the following are determined (weighted by length, integrated by the trapezoidal rule on the grid Δs):

$$V_{p,sr} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L V_p(s)\,ds \approx \frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \frac{V_i + V_{i+1}}{2}\,\Delta s_i$$

$$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \left(V_p(s) - V_{p,sr}\right)^2 ds}$$

$$D_h = \frac{\sigma}{V_{p,sr}} \cdot 100\ [\%]$$

The dynamic consistency of adjacent alignment elements (tangent – curve – tangent) is expressed by the difference of projected speeds

$$\Delta V_{i,i+1} = \left| V_{p,i} - V_{p,i+1} \right|$$

Rating criterion (Lamm et al. [5]): ΔV ≤ 10 km/h – good; 10 < ΔV ≤ 20 km/h – fair; ΔV > 20 km/h – poor. The projected speed of an element is taken as: on a circular curve (with transition curves) the lowest speed, on a tangent the highest speed in the element.
